questions.question: Which one of the following techniques is not used in the binary tree?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Binary trees are traversed by preorder, inorder, postorder and level-order traversals; randomized traversal is not a standard binary tree technique.

questions.question: Routing involves:

options.C: Determining the best path for data packets

questions.explanation: Routing is the process of determining the best path for data packets across networks. Framing, flow control and error correction are data link functions.

questions.question: In a binary search tree, which subtree of a node contains elements that are greater than the node's value?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In a BST, all keys in the right subtree are greater than the node, and all keys in the left subtree are smaller.

questions.question: The term HTTP stands for:
questions.explanation: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, used to transfer web pages between server and browser.

questions.question: The recurrence equation T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 represents the time complexity of which algorithmic paradigm?
questions.explanation: T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 halves the problem at each step with constant combining work, as in binary search, a divide and conquer algorithm; it solves to O(log n). Greedy and brute force do not split the input recursively.

questions.question: What is the term for a variable that references an instance of a class?
questions.explanation: A variable that refers to an instance of a class is an object (object reference). Properties and methods are members of a class, and a constructor initialises the object.

questions.question: Which of the following is the prefix form of A+B*C?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Since * has higher precedence, B*C becomes *BC, and then A + (*BC) becomes +A*BC. ABC*+ would be the postfix form.

questions.question: The process of acquiring a semaphore and entering a critical section while ensuring mutual exclusion is often called:
questions.explanation: Acquiring a semaphore before entering a critical section to guarantee mutual exclusion is critical section synchronization. Lock-free and wait-free techniques avoid locks, and barriers make threads wait for each other at a point.

questions.question: Divide and Conquer is an algorithmic paradigm that solves problems by:
questions.explanation: Divide and conquer splits a problem into smaller subproblems, solves them recursively, and combines the results (e.g. merge sort). Greedy choice and heuristics belong to other paradigms.

questions.question: Subnetting allows for:
questions.explanation: Subnetting divides a network into smaller subnetworks so IP addresses are allocated more efficiently with less waste. Security and speed gains are side benefits, not its main purpose.

questions.question: In the Divide and Conquer algorithm for finding the maximum and minimum elements, how are the results from the left and right subarrays combined?

options.A: By taking the average of the maximum and minimum values
options.B: By comparing the maximum of the left and right subarrays and the minimum of the left and right subarrays
options.C: By adding the maximum of the left subarray to the minimum of the right subarray
options.D: By multiplying the maximum of the left subarray with the minimum of the right subarray

questions.explanation: The overall max is the larger of the two sub-maxima and the overall min is the smaller of the two sub-minima, costing 2 comparisons. Averaging, adding or multiplying values does not give extremes.

questions.question: Which of the following attributes is not a valid attribute of the <body> tag in HTML?
questions.explanation: The (legacy) <body> tag supports text, background, bgcolor, link, alink and vlink, but not width.

questions.question: Select the correct option to fill in the blank: A ___________ is an online platform or website where individuals or businesses regularly publish articles/journals, known as posts, on various topics.
questions.explanation: A blog is a website where an individual or business regularly publishes posts. A browser is software for viewing websites and a web server hosts them.

questions.concept: Deletion at rear in singly linked list
questions.question: In the deque implementation, using singly linked list, what would be the time complexity of deleting an element from the rear end?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: To delete the rear node of a singly linked list we must find its predecessor by traversing from the head, which takes O(N). O(1) applies to deletion from the front.

questions.question: Which version control system is commonly used for collaborative web development projects?
questions.explanation: Git is the most widely used distributed version control system for collaborative web development (e.g. via GitHub). SVN, Mercurial and CVS exist but are far less common today.

questions.question:
Statement A: Knowledge base (KB) consists of a set of statements.
Statement B: Inference is deriving a new sentence from the KB.
Choose the correct option.

options.A: A is True, B is True
options.B: A is False, B is False
options.C: A is True, B is false
options.D: A is false, B is True

questions.explanation: A knowledge base is a set of sentences (statements) in a knowledge representation language, and inference is the process of deriving new sentences from the KB. Both statements are true.

questions.question: The concept of NP-Completeness was introduced by:
questions.explanation: Stephen Cook introduced NP-completeness in 1971 (Cook's theorem, proving SAT NP-complete). Richard Karp extended it in 1972 by showing 21 problems NP-complete, so he popularised but did not introduce the concept.

questions.question: In a system with a page size of 4 KB and a physical address space of 64 GB, what is the number of bits required for the page offset?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The offset must address every byte within a page: 4 KB = 2^12 bytes, so 12 bits are needed. The physical memory size does not affect the offset width.

questions.question: Which protocol assigns IP address to the client connected in the internet?
questions.explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns IP addresses to clients. IP only carries packets.

questions.question: In Real Time Interactive Audio Video, Jitter is introduced in real-time data by delay between____
questions.explanation: Jitter arises because successive packets of real-time data experience different delays across the network. Pixels, layers and frames are not the unit of delay variation.

questions.question: Regular expression for all strings that start with b and end with bba is:
questions.explanation: b(a+b)*bba starts with b, allows any string in the middle, and ends with bba. Options A and B start with a, so they cannot describe strings starting with b.

questions.question: Abstraction means
questions.explanation: Abstraction means showing only the essential features and hiding the background (implementation) details from the user. Summarization is a loose description, but the defining idea is hiding complexity.

questions.question: Which one is a communication channel security protocol?
questions.explanation: SSL secures the transport channel, S-HTTP secures HTTP messages, and SET secures card payment transactions; all three are communication channel security protocols in e-commerce.

questions.question: In general, a file is basically a collection of all related______.
questions.explanation: In the data hierarchy, fields form records and a file is a collection of related records. Fields are one level below records.

questions.question: What happens when you press Ctrl + X after selecting some cells in Excel?

options.A: The cell content of selected cells disappears from the cells and is stored in the clipboard
options.B: The cells selected are marked for cutting
options.C: The selected cells are deleted and the cells are shifted left
options.D: The selected cells are deleted and cells are shifted up

questions.explanation: In Excel, Ctrl+X does not remove content immediately; the selected cells get a moving border (marquee) marking them for cutting until you paste.
